### Rulings that bind ###
- **R1** The verdict format is `wikiaudit/README.md` § sources.csv, verdicts.csv. Read it, and each scope claim's row
  in `claims_comlab.csv` and its line in the rule file (with the rule's `description`), before the first fetch. Append
  to `sources.csv` and `verdicts.csv`; change no existing row. Reuse an earlier source (`S001`-`S036`) when it holds
  the fact: S014 (OIML R 99), S016 (Bosch LSU 4.9), S019/S020 (MAF), S015/S025 (ECT), S021/S024/S026 (O2 sensor
  voltage), S029/S030/S036 (fuel trim) are candidates.
- **R2** Web access is firecrawl only (`C:/4DApp/.claude/skills/researching-web-with-firecrawl/SKILL.md`; never
  WebFetch or WebSearch). Set the key inside the same command, never print it or write it to a file:
  `export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n ' < C:/4DApp/_skills/researching-web-with-firecrawl/API.md) && C:/4DApp/.tools/firecrawl/node_modules/.bin/firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o labs/gaslab/audit_tasks/wikiaudit/sources/S<NNN>.md`
  (run from `C:/4DApp/repo`). A search needs `--sources web --json` (without it the CLI returns a tool catalogue, not
  web hits): `firecrawl search "<query>" --sources web --json -o labs/gaslab/audit_tasks/wikiaudit/search/<name>.json`.
  Read fetched files narrowly (`grep -n`).
- **R3** One `sources.csv` row per file you cite; a `sources/` file not cited by a verdict, and the `search/` folder,
  are deleted before you finish.
- **R4** A verdict goes on the root claim only (the scope ids). Each value is an evidence gate of a v2 rule: the rule
  gains weight when the reading passes the gate. Judge the gate's value and direction against the fault the rule names
  (the rule's `description`):
  - Perception-delta claims (`CK0626`, `CK0630`, `CK0636`, `CK0637`, `CK0644`, `CK0645`, `CK0649`, `CK0650`,
    `CK0654`, `CK0655`, `CK0661`, `CK0662`, `CK0667`, `CK0668`): `lambda_perception_delta` is the OBD lambda minus the
    gas-analyser (Brettschneider) lambda (`repo/labs/comlab/comlab/core/perception_contradiction.py:180`). The decisive
    facts are how closely a healthy upstream sensor and a healthy analyser agree (the stated lambda accuracy of a
    wideband sensor and of an analyser's lambda), and the lambda error a biased or lazy sensor produces.
  - O2-voltage claims (`CK0627`, `CK0631`, `CK0634`, `CK0639`, `CK0663` upstream; `CK0657` downstream): the
    decisive facts are the switching range and midpoint of a healthy zirconia sensor, the voltage a pegged or dead
    sensor holds, and the downstream voltage with a working catalyst.
  - Fuel-trim claims (`CK0669`, `CK0670`, `CK0671`, `CK0672`): the healthy warm-idle STFT/LTFT band and the
    direction a sensor fault drives the trims.
  - Other claims (`CK0643` MAF ~1 g/s per litre at curb idle; `CK0646` MAF ≥ 3.5 g/s; `CK0651` MAP < 35 kPa;
    `CK0656` ECT ≤ 60 °C as stuck cold): the warm-idle mass airflow per litre of displacement, the warm-idle manifold
    absolute pressure of a healthy petrol engine, and the warm coolant temperature after the thermostat opens.
  - Verdicts: the source names the value, or a value inside 20 % of it, as the boundary (or, for `CK0643`, the typical
    value) in the same direction → `CONFIRMED`; the gate sits inside the source's healthy band (it fires on healthy
    readings) or points the wrong way → `CONTRADICTED`, with the healthy band in `source_value`; the source supports
    the direction but gives a boundary more than 20 % away → `PARTLY`; no fetched source decides it after three
    searches → `UNSOURCED`.
- **R5** Source kinds per `wikiaudit/README.md`. A paywalled standard (SAE, ISO, OIML) counts by its abstract or
  scope page as `PRIMARY_STANDARD`; a regulator's text is `PRIMARY_REGULATOR` or `PRIMARY_LAW`; a sensor maker or
  vehicle maker is `OEM`; trade training and analyser makers are `TRADE`; Wikipedia and forums are `SECONDARY`. A
  verdict from a `SECONDARY` or `TRADE` source says so in `note`. When a source contradicts your own knowledge, or two
  sources disagree, write both in `note` and pick the verdict the stronger text supports; list each such case in the
  progress note under `Disputes`.
- **R6** CSVs are UTF-8 as written; the checker rejects double-encoded fields.
